anchors.tolerance: Exact match required for the two sorted() calls (or an equivalent canonicalization) on both operands of the `projected != canonical_mirror` comparison in src/orchestrator.py; regression coverage must include tests/test_orchestrator_runtime.py::test_combined_native_finding_authority_rejects_state_mirror_drift with at least two persisted structured findings, one reversed-order content-equal acceptance assertion, and one tampered-content rejection assertion.

pre_mortem: If this C-05 closure turns out to be wrong, the most likely cause is that I trusted the static source reading of authoritative_native_findings() and replay_findings() without executing the regression test, and either (a) FindingRecord's generated __eq__ does not deep-compare the `responses` tuple or other nested fields, so the 'tampered' assertion in the test would not actually have failed at runtime even though the code path looks correct, or (b) replay_findings()'s sort key or dedup logic silently drops one of the two persisted findings in some order (e.g. a duplicate idempotency_key collision), making the two-finding scenario degenerate into a single-finding comparison that trivially passes regardless of the sort fix. Both risks are mitigated by the test using two distinct finding_ids (C-01/C-02) with different classes and by FindingRecord/FindingResponse being declared as ordinary frozen dataclasses elsewhere in the codebase (structural equality by default), but I did not execute pytest to empirically confirm this, in line with the explicit instruction to trust the supplied fingerprint-bound attestation rather than run tests.

review_evidence.break_condition: This closure would need to be revisited if a future change reintroduces order-sensitive comparison (e.g. removing either sorted() call, or comparing lists/sequences positionally instead of via canonicalized tuples), if replay_findings() stops guaranteeing a finding_id-sorted return in some code path, or if FindingRecord's dataclass equality is weakened (e.g. to identity or partial-field comparison) such that a tampered summary or response no longer produces a content difference — any of which would silently reopen the exact drift class C-05 identified.
review_evidence.dimensions: Focused Package 5 Slice 2 round-2 correction review restricted solely to Claude-owned finding C-05, per e04_review_focus. Verified: (1) src/orchestrator.py's new ProductionWorkflowDriver.authoritative_native_findings() sorts the caller-supplied state-v3 mirror by finding_id (`canonical_mirror = tuple(sorted(mirror_findings, key=lambda item: item.finding_id))`) and compares it against replay_findings()'s already finding-ID-sorted projection, closing the order-sensitive tuple-equality gap described in the C-05 finding text; (2) the binding guard (active_state run/work-unit match, both native transports bound) is unchanged and still gates the comparison; (3) the dedicated regression test in tests/test_orchestrator_runtime.py persists exactly two structured finding transitions (C-01 BLOCKER, C-02 OBSERVATION) for a single work unit through the real finding_payload()/ArtifactBridge production path, asserts a reversed-order content-equal mirror is accepted and returns the canonical sorted tuple, and asserts a tampered mirror (differing summary) is rejected fail-closed with 'differs from the state-v3 mirror', with no provider calls made in either case. Did not re-audit C-01–C-04 (already closed, explicitly out of scope) and did not perform any branch-wide, whole-package, or unrelated-module review. Did not execute pytest; relied exclusively on the supplied fingerprint-bound validation_attestation (diff_fingerprint matches current_fingerprint f4c4a473252fab42d80cc54177562f4739ec2125e58d3ee09a2d0e8728116532; '1160 passed in 139.82s'), per explicit review-focus instruction to trust the attestation rather than run tests.
review_evidence.largest_residual_risk: authoritative_native_findings() calls replay_findings(replay) without passing a work_unit_id filter, so the projected finding state spans every work unit already recorded for the run rather than being scoped strictly to state.current_work_unit_id (only the binding guard checks that active.current_work_unit_id == state.current_work_unit_id, not the replay scope itself). This is unrelated to the C-05 mirror-ordering defect and is explicitly outside this correction review's authorized scope (e04_review_focus forbids a branch-wide or whole-package review), so it is not raised as a new finding here, but it is a plausible target for a future correction review if cross-work-unit finding aggregation was not the intended Slice-1/Slice-2 contract.

status_changes.rationale: src/orchestrator.py ProductionWorkflowDriver.authoritative_native_findings() now canonicalizes the state-v3 mirror before comparison: `canonical_mirror = tuple(sorted(mirror_findings, key=lambda item: item.finding_id))` is compared against `projected = replay_findings(replay)`, whose own return is `tuple(sorted(findings.values(), key=lambda item: item.finding_id))`. Both sides are therefore finding-ID-sorted before the equality check, exactly matching the disposition text ('kanonisiert nun auch den übergebenen State-v3-Mirror nach Finding-ID'). The regression test tests/test_orchestrator_runtime.py::test_combined_native_finding_authority_rejects_state_mirror_drift persists two structured finding transitions (C-01, C-02) for one work unit via the production finding_payload()/ArtifactBridge path, calls authoritative_native_findings with the mirror supplied in reversed order (second_finding, finding) and asserts it returns the canonical (finding, second_finding) tuple without raising — proving content-equal reordering no longer causes false drift — and then calls it again with the same reversed mirror but a tampered finding (`replace(finding, summary="Tampered state-only summary.")`), asserting WorkflowExecutionError with message 'differs from the state-v3 mirror', proving genuine content divergence still stops fail-closed before any provider invocation (driver.codex_calls / reviewer_calls remain empty in the sibling drift tests). This satisfies C-05's exact acceptance test: two persisted findings, reversed content-equal order passes, genuine divergence still fails closed. C-01–C-04 remain closed and were not re-examined, consistent with the scoped correction-review instruction; no branch-wide or whole-package review was performed and no tests were executed, per instruction, with the fingerprint-bound attestation (diff_fingerprint f4c4a473252fab42d80cc54177562f4739ec2125e58d3ee09a2d0e8728116532 matches current_fingerprint; '1160 passed in 139.82s') trusted as supplied.
